rows.name: player_x_position (Mario's horizontal level position within the page, low byte)
rows.notes: Encoding: one byte, Mario's horizontal position within the current 256-pixel page; absolute level x = 0x006D*256 + 0x0086 (World 1-1 starts at 0x006D=0, 0x0086=40=0x28, and his on-screen sprite x = absolute x - camera). Found with no reference by differential search: three walking rounds (diff 'increased' 172 -> 57 -> 22 survivors) kept 0x0086, which rose ~1.5 px/frame; a 60-frame play_input watch showed it climb 244->255 then wrap to 0 and continue to 49 while the camera (0x073F) only reached 66, so a separate page byte had to exist. Proof by write_memory + screenshot: while paused, wrote 0x0086=150 (was 69) and stepped 2 frames - Mario's OAM entries (read with list_sprites) moved from screen x=0 to x=81 with the camera still at 69 (screenshot: Mario stands further right, next to the first Goomba). A second write 0x0086=200 with the camera at 114 put his OAM at screen x=86 = 200-114. Source: differential search.

rows.name: player_x_page (page / high byte of Mario's horizontal level position)
rows.notes: Encoding: one byte, the page/high byte of Mario's horizontal level position; absolute level x = 0x006D*256 + 0x0086. Found with no reference by differential search: a 60-frame play_input watch showed 0x006D tick 0->1 at the exact frame 0x0086 wrapped 255->0, and a snapshot diff across a real crossing (q1->q2) reproduced it - 0x006D 0->1 while 0x0086 251->38 and the camera was still on page 0 at 113 - so it is the player's page, not the camera's. Proof by write_memory + screenshot: with the camera fixed at 114 and 0x0086=200 (page 0) Mario's OAM x read 86; after write_memory 0x006D=1 with 0x0086=100 and stepping, RAM kept 0x006D=1 / 0x0086=97 and Mario's OAM x jumped to 239 = (256+97)-114 (screenshot: Mario at the right edge of the screen, i.e. +256 level pixels despite a lower low byte). Note: setting a page more than one ahead of the camera's page (i.e. placing his computed screen x off the 0-255 range) makes the engine snap Mario back to the camera's left edge, so the proof uses a one-page step. Source: differential search.

rows.name: Mario's horizontal position: absolute level x = $006D*256 + $0086
rows.notes: World 1-1. The player's level x is a 16-bit-ish pair: page at 0x006D and within-page byte at 0x0086 (absolute x = 0x006D*256 + 0x0086). On-screen sprite x = absolute x - camera, where the camera left edge low byte is 0x071C (0x071A = its page) and 0x073F/0x0740 are the scroll bytes the NMI writes to PPUSCROLL. Both bytes are canonical: a write to 0x0086 persists across frames and moves the sprite, and a one-page write to 0x006D moves it by 256. Caveat: if a hand-written page puts the computed screen x outside 0-255 (more than one page ahead of the camera), the engine snaps Mario back to the camera's left edge, which is why the page proof uses a one-page step. Found with no reference via differential search (walk-right increased/wrap + writes), session 2026-10-09.
